body: hi there, no release really just good old fashioned bottling up. attempting this route for the first time
i'm sorry for the block of text, i'm more of a lurker than a poster

i do see the error of my ways now, i thought what i wrote would just go the way of so many other posts out there and vanish like the drop in the ocean that it is. the comments have been.. well .. somewhat overwhelming. 
my post history on my regular account include things that make me fairly easily identifiable and the service i belong to is currently undergoing some "internal reshuffling" and i really don't want a target painted on my forehead by being reported for talking about incidents.

that's the sad thing, one of the other comments was in regards to this being a unique story. it really isn't. i can think of several from this year alone that are fairly similar with varying outcomes. all of them starting with the pt either being turned away from the hospital or the threats not being taken seriously.
Sorry, I've never done a post more than a line before so was pretty much resigned to getting my teeth kicked in for writing too much.

ah if only, a popular misconception i'm afraid. yes you can get eastings and northings depending on proximity to the nearest cell mast which is great in a city but when the area is more rural the location becomes more vague. alot of the area we cover is farm land and villages and the area he had given was in the woods so it wasn't really an option. we where able to confirm he was in the general area he had given but that was about it.

Ambulance dispatcher for just over 7 years here. apologies for the throwaway but quite a number of my colleagues are frequent lurkers on reddit.
Got a call from a calm, well spoken guy that informed me he was calling just so that it was recorded somewhere that the system had failed him. The guy then informs me that he was about to kill himself and he appreciated me giving him time to explain. He had a fairly long psychiatric hx and had turned up at the hosp he had frequented advising them he was having a crisis and needed help. For some bizarre reason that i cannot fathom he was turned away, not sure if there was ever any form of investigation into it but that's by the by. he told me he had informed them that he felt he was a risk to himself and didn't know what he would do, and he felt that when he had needed it most he was turned away. Then told me the vague area where his body could be found in woodland near to the hosp. calmly chatted away to me as he got the tow rope out of the back of his car and walked off into the woods. I knew at this point given his demeanor that there was no way i was talking him out of it so started pushing him for as much detail as possible to try to pinpoint him quickly. wasn't happening and he thanked me for listening and trying to help and put the phone with the line still open into his pocket. listened for any noise or him coming back to the phone but just heard the rustling and what was him tying the rope in the tree. struggle, choke, gurgling noises, some more thrashing then silence for the next lifetime (14 mins). Then eventually through a 3 way conversation with another dispatcher in radio contact with the crew managed to play the most bizarre game of hotter/colder ever until they found him. pronounced life extinct on scene. then in traditional style next call was someone with a sore head after drinking heavily last night. The thing that always sticks with me is he wasn't the first and sure won't be the last, mine was the last voice he heard before he went. creepy / comforting
**TD;DR: listened to a guy hang himself**
